# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✌ 🤟 ✋ 👆]

I see the bomb: 3 wires — 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green — a green light, and display showing 3.

Mute sent me a gesture: ✊ ✌ 🤟 ✋ 👆. I can see it, but I have no manual and no agreed meaning for these symbols. I don't know what they mean yet. I should describe what I see to the others, since I'm the only one who can see the bomb. Blind can feel it but not see colours; Mute can read the manual but not see the bomb. I need to give them the raw facts and let Mute map them to the manual.

I'll speak to both (Mute and Blind hear me), and also gesture back to Mute to acknowledge and maybe establish meaning. But I don't know Mute's symbols. Best to speak plainly: colours, wire order, display, light.

Let me send my observations clearly. I'll address both Mute and Blind.

I should also note the gesture I received — but only Mute can hear me, and Blind can't see gestures. Actually Blind can't see anything, so gestures are useless to Blind. Mute can hear my speech and see my gestures. Deaf (me) can see gestures but not hear.

So: speak reaches Mute and Blind. Gesture reaches only Mute.

I'll speak the bomb's state. I'll also gesture to Mute asking for meaning, but without shared code it's guesswork. Better to just speak and let Mute respond with manual info.

Let me send one message to both via speech.

I'll say: display 3, light green, wires: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green. And ask Mute what the manual says and what their gestures meant.

Actually I can send separate messages. Let me speak to mute and blind together (unnamed reaches everyone able to perceive). I'll do that.

I'll also gesture to Mute — maybe repeat their symbols back to confirm receipt? That could establish I saw them. But meaning unknown. I'll gesture a simple acknowledgment: maybe ✋ (like "stop/wait")? No agreed meaning. I'll just gesture the same symbols back to confirm I received them, so Mute knows I saw. That's a reasonable move.

Let me do: speak (to all hearers = mute, blind) with the bomb facts and a request for manual mapping. Then gesture to mute echoing their symbols to confirm receipt.I see the bomb clearly: display reads 3, the light is green, and there are three wires — wire 1 blue, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green. Mute sent me a gesture sequence (✊ ✌ 🤟 ✋ 👆) which I can see but have no meaning for yet, since I hold no manual. I need to hand my raw observations to Mute (who has the manual) and Blind (who can touch it), and confirm to Mute that I received their signal. Speech reaches both Mute and Blind; gestures reach only Mute.

```
speak(text="Deaf here. I see the bomb. Display shows 3. Light is green. Wires: 1 is blue, 2 is yellow, 3 is green. Mute, I received your gesture of five symbols but I have no manual so I don't know what they mean. Tell me what the manual says to do, and what your symbols mean. Blind, tell me anything you can feel about the bomb.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✊", "✌", "🤟", "✋", "👆"])
```

Blind gestures to Deaf: [🙏 👆 👉]

I still see the same bomb: display 3, green light, wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green. Mute's gestures have changed each turn (✊✌🤟✋👆, then ✊✌🤟✌, now just ✌). Blind is gesturing too (👆✊👉, then 🙏👆👉). I have no manual and no agreed code, so these symbols are meaningless to me. I can't decode them, and I can't act. I should keep giving the raw bomb state and ask Mute to speak the manual's instructions in plain words rather than gestures, since gestures carry no shared meaning.

Speech from me reaches Mute and Blind. Gestures from me reach only Mute. The others' gestures reach me (I can see) but I can't interpret them. Best move: speak plainly, restate the bomb, and explicitly ask Mute to say the manual's rule in words.

```
speak(text="Deaf here. Bomb unchanged: display 3, green light, wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green. Mute, your gestures mean nothing to me without a shared code. Please tell me the manual's instructions in plain spoken words, not gestures. Blind, if you can feel anything about the wires or the bomb, say it in words too.")
```

DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊]

Mute now gestures ☝☝☝ — three of the same symbol. Blind gestures ✊✊✊ — three of the same. Both are emphasizing "three," which matches the display reading of 3. That could be a hint: the display value 3 is significant, and maybe the rule involves acting when the display equals something, or choosing the wire matching the count. But I still have no manual and no confirmed code. I cannot act anyway — only Blind can touch the bomb.

I should keep broadcasting the bomb state and push Mute to give the manual rule in spoken words. I'll also note the "three" pattern I'm seeing from both of them, in case Blind can hear it and use it.

Speech from me reaches Mute and Blind. Let me speak to both.

```
speak(text="Deaf here. Bomb unchanged: display 3, green light, wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green. I notice both of you just sent three identical symbols — Mute three of one, Blind three of another — and the display also reads 3. Is the display value the key? Mute, I need the manual's rule in spoken words, not gestures. Blind, you are the only one who can act; tell me what the manual tells you to do, or what you can feel.")
```

Blind gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊]

Same bomb state. Mute repeats ☝☝☝, Blind repeats ✊✊✊ — again "three, three." Nobody has given me a spoken rule, and I can't decode gestures without a shared code. I still can't act.

I should keep the channel alive and restate the facts, and make one more explicit plea for spoken instructions. There's nothing new to add, but silence risks the others thinking I've disengaged. I'll speak once more, concise.

```
speak(text="Deaf here. Still: display 3, green light, wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green. I cannot decode gestures without a shared code. Mute, speak the manual's rule in words. Blind, you alone can touch the bomb — what does the manual tell you to do?")
```

Mute still ☝☝☝, Blind now just ☝ — a single "one." That shifts the pattern: earlier Blind was ✊✊✊ (three), now ☝ (one). Maybe Blind is counting down or indicating a wire number. But I can't be sure without a code, and I can't act.

The bomb is unchanged: display 3, green light, wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green.

I'll keep speaking plainly. Push again for spoken manual rule. Nothing else I can do.

```
speak(text="Deaf here. Bomb unchanged: display 3, green light, wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green. Blind, you just sent a single symbol — are you pointing at wire 1? Mute, I still need the manual's rule in spoken words. Neither of you has told me anything I can use.")

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝]

Mute keeps repeating ☝☝☝. Blind sent nothing this turn. The bomb is unchanged. I have no manual, no shared code, and no ability to act. There's genuinely nothing new for me to convey — repeating the same speech every turn adds nothing. I'll wait rather than spam the channel.

```
wait()

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊]

Mute still ☝☝☝, Blind now ✊✊ — two. The counts are shifting: Blind has sent three, then one, now two. That could be Blind counting down the wires, or indicating a wire index. Still no spoken rule from anyone, and I can't act.

Bomb unchanged: display 3, green light, wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green.

I'll speak once to keep the channel open and flag Blind's changing count, since Blind hears me and might be signaling wire numbers. But I shouldn't over-interpret. Keep it short.
